purpose: X01: accepted LTRA history must be unchanged by rejected trial steps, observed on a curved waveform where every history entry is distinct.

oracle.derivation: Rs=Z0 so GammaS=0. SIN(0 1 62.5meg) into Z0=50, Td=10 ns, RL=150 with CL=1 pF: ZL=1/(1/RL+jwCL)=149.481332245-8.805177286j, GammaL=(ZL-Z0)/(ZL+Z0)=0.499674778-0.022084534j. v(b)=Im[0.5(1+GammaL)exp(-jwTd)exp(jwt)] for t>Td and 0 before; v(a)=0.5 sin(wt) for t<2Td (incident only) and Im[0.5(1+GammaL exp(-2jwTd))exp(jwt)] after. The load RC transient (tau=(RL||Z0)CL=37.5 ps) is dead by the first sample after Td. reltol=1e-8/vntol=1e-12/abstol=1e-15 with no user tmax forces the LTE controller to shrink, reject and retry: 2966 accepted points against 2258 with the .options line deleted, same values to 5.4e-6, both under the 8192 history bound. The 15 ns row (Td<t<2Td) is the one a plateau-driven deck cannot express: v(a) must still be the pure incident -0.191342 while v(b) is already +0.696985. The 5e-5 band is set by the runner's linear interpolation between 20 ps output points, (h^2/8)|v''|=3.9e-6; a trial value leaking into the accepted history moves v(b) by order 0.1-0.9 V.
oracle.cross_check: Independent ngspice-44.2 run of this exact netlist agrees with all 18 hand values to 5.3e-6; the checkpoint binary to 5.4e-6 (this fixture passes today and is a regression gate).
